data.description:
## Context (placeholder — to be brainstormed)

DSO is, in the framing of Böckeler/Fowler's 'Harness Engineering for Coding Agents' (martinfowler.com/articles/harness-engineering.html), a mature agent HARNESS: an outer layer of guides (feedforward — CLAUDE.md rules, SKILL.md files, contracts) and SENSORS (feedback — ~40 hooks, pre-commit gates, CI llm-review, completion-verifier, the workflow-stability checks). The project has invested heavily in adding sensors but has no systematic way to evaluate the harness AS A WHOLE.

The article names two unsolved challenges this epic targets directly:

1. INTERPRETING SILENT SENSORS — 'do silent sensors indicate quality or inadequate detection?' A gate that has not fired in weeks is ambiguous: either the codebase is clean (good) or the gate is blind/misconfigured/dead (bad). DSO ships new checks in warn -> enforce mode, and the warn->enforce promotion decision is currently made on intuition rather than evidence of the gate actually catching things.

2. EVALUATING HARNESS COVERAGE SYSTEMATICALLY — the article calls out the absence of frameworks for treating scattered controls as one integrated system. DSO's sensor telemetry today exists only in per-sensor fragments (see Related), never across the whole gate+hook suite.

## Goal

Give the DSO maintainer a single, evidence-based view of SENSOR HEALTH across the entire harness, so that:
- Dead/silent gates are detected (fired 0 times over a window) and surfaced for retirement-or-fix triage, resolving the article's silent-sensor ambiguity with data instead of intuition.
- Per-gate signal quality is measured (fire count, true-positive vs false-positive/dismissed/overridden rate, time-since-last-fire) so high-noise gates can be tuned and the warn->enforce promotion decision is driven by observed catch evidence.
- Harness COVERAGE is assessable: what classes of agent failure does the current sensor set actually catch, and where are the blind spots — the article's 'evaluate harness coverage systematically' challenge.

This is the harness-level rollup that the existing per-sensor telemetry epics do not provide; it consumes their signals rather than replacing them.

## Scope (to be brainstormed via /dso:brainstorm)

Likely components (NOT yet committed):
- A gate/hook firing-event emission convention (each hook/gate emits a structured fired/passed/false-positive record) — or a passive scan over existing hook logs (tool-logging.sh, commit-failure-tracker, review defenses).
- A periodic sensor-health report: per-gate fire count, FP/override rate, days-since-last-fire, with a 'silent sensor' flag and a warn->enforce readiness signal.
- Integration touchpoint with /dso:retro (which already does shift-left 'was this catchable earlier' classification) as the natural consumption surface.

## Related (consumes / coordinates, does not duplicate)

- c13f-6196 (Test gate observability) — per-gate FP/phantom detection scoped to the ONE pre-commit test gate; this epic generalizes the pattern across all gates.
- 5df7-63ac (Integrated observability: context/cost/agent telemetry) — supplies a telemetry store + rotation that this epic's report could read; that epic is session/cost-framed, not harness-sensor-health-framed.
- spiky-stand-chick (Code review telemetry dashboard) — review-sensor ROI; one sensor only.
- tough-mouse-stand / pop-hatch-hoop (calibration program health rollups) — test-quality/mutation sensors only.
- tap-folly-phase (411b mutation-testing) — its kill-rate telemetry is one sensor's health signal that this rollup would surface; see the harness-engineering framing comment on 411b.

## Dependencies

SOFT (coordination): 5df7-63ac telemetry store likely provides the substrate; sequence brainstorm after its shape is known. No hard blockers.

## Out of scope (pre-brainstorm intent)

- Building new GATES (this epic measures existing sensors, it does not add detection logic).
- Replacing per-sensor calibration programs (review, test-quality, mutation) — this rolls them up, it does not absorb them.
data.title: Harness sensor-health observability: detect silent/dead gates and per-gate signal quality across the full gate+hook suite
